title: 'Surrounded': Israel's new West Bank settlements bring chaos to Palestinians
gist: The Netanyahu government's 2026 legalization and reoccupation of previously evacuated northern West Bank settlement sites, including a December plan legalizing 17 new settlements explicitly meant to connect them, is triggering land seizures, shop demolitions and new military bases even inside nominally Palestinian-controlled Areas A and B, undermining the Oslo Accords' territorial division.

insights.claim: The UN's Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs recorded an average of six settler-related incidents per day across the West Bank in 2026, including theft, vandalism, arson, beatings and sometimes murder, with Palestinians saying most crimes go unpunished.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A hard daily-incident rate gives a quantifiable baseline for tracking whether West Bank settler violence is escalating or stabilizing over time.
insights.locator: the UN's Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

insights.claim: Palestinian farmer Amin Rahal and his three brothers have stopped going to work for weeks to guard their land from settlers of the newly inaugurated Emek Dotan settlement 100 metres away, who have stolen hens, seized land with olive trees, and cordoned off part of his property with a rope forbidding him from crossing.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Illustrates the direct economic loss (livelihood, land, crops) inflicted on individual Palestinian households by new settlement outposts.
insights.quote: They've stolen hens, land with olive trees, damaged the sage bush in our backyard with their ATVs, brought their sheep into our courtyard, and more
insights.locator: Last week, settlers from the newly inaugurated Israeli settlement

themes.theme: Reoccupation of evacuated sites and Oslo rollback

insights.claim: Under Ariel Sharon's 2005 disengagement plan, four isolated settlements — Homesh, Sa-Nur, Ganim and Kadim — were evacuated to create a contiguous Palestinian space in the northern West Bank, but under the current Netanyahu government the abandoned sites have been reoccupied one by one during 2026.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The reversal of a 2005 land-for-continuity settlement evacuation marks a structural shift in West Bank policy that materially narrows any future contiguous Palestinian territory.
insights.locator: Under former Israeli prime minister Ariel Sharon's 2005

insights.claim: A plan approved in December legalized 17 more settlements in the northern West Bank with the specific intent of connecting them, which the article frames as another affront to the Oslo Accords.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A deliberate settlement-connection strategy signals an intent to consolidate territorial control in the north, a leading indicator for further Palestinian displacement there.
insights.locator: A plan approved in December legalised 17 more settlements

insights.claim: Under the Oslo Accords, Israel was permitted to build settlements and demolish Palestinian buildings only in Area C, the roughly 60% of the West Bank under full Israeli control, an arrangement Israel's far-right — including Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, himself a settler — has repeatedly called to 'cancel.'
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A senior sitting minister publicly calling to scrap Oslo's territorial division is a direct policy signal that Area A/B protections may erode further.
insights.locator: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, himself a settler

insights.claim: A new Israeli military base was established inside Jenin itself, in Area A, the part of the West Bank supposed to be under full Palestinian control, and settler caravans near Ganim and Kadim have been connected to the electric grid and received their first occupants.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Military and settlement infrastructure appearing inside nominally Palestinian-controlled Area A marks an expansion of Israeli presence beyond the areas Oslo assigned it, a concrete territorial-control indicator.
insights.locator: Inside Jenin itself, the largest city

insights.claim: Israeli forces demolished several shops near the road leading to Ganim and Kadim in August, including stone-products store owner Bara al-Damaj's shop, after issuing an official evacuation order followed immediately by demolition.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Rapid demolition with minimal notice period demonstrates the pace and finality with which Israeli authorities are clearing land for settlement expansion.
insights.quote: In a moment, they destroyed our dreams
insights.locator: They came to us directly and gave us an official order

insights.claim: Army bulldozers have blocked agricultural roads with rubble near Jenin, cutting off Palestinian farmers from their fields, and in the village of Deir Abu Deif losing access to the blocked road also means losing access to the city of Jenin.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Road-blocking as a de facto isolation tactic threatens the economic viability of whole villages dependent on access to the regional urban hub.
insights.quote: The situation is extremely frightening. We're surrounded from every direction
insights.locator: In the village of Deir Abu Deif

insights.claim: Armed settlement security teams have begun conducting ID checks on Palestinian residents near Jenin as if they were official authorities, with one resident describing a white van used for this purpose as terrorizing the entire eastern area of the city.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Private settlement security forces exercising quasi-governmental authority over Palestinians outside legal settlement boundaries signals a further erosion of formal rule of law in the area.
insights.quote: This white van terrorises us and the entire eastern area
